ESV.1: King Solomon was king over all Israel,
ESV.2: and these were his high officials: Azariah the son of Zadok was the priest;
ESV.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah the sons of Shisha were secretaries; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was recorder;
ESV.4: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
ESV.5: Azariah the son of Nathan was over the officers; Zabud the son of Nathan was priest and king's friend;
ESV.6: Ahishar was in charge of the palace; and Adoniram the son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.
ESV.7: Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided food for the king and his household. Each man had to make provision for one month in the year.
ESV.8: These were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
ESV.9: Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elonbeth-hanan;
ESV.10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth (to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher);
ESV.11: Ben-abinadab, in all Naphath-dor (he had Taphath the daughter of Solomon as his wife);
ESV.12: Baana the son of Ahilud, in Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shean that is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, and from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as the other side of Jokmeam;
ESV.13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead (he had the villages of Jair the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, and he had the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);
ESV.14: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
ESV.15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he had taken Basemath the daughter of Solomon as his wife);
ESV.16: Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
ESV.17: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
ESV.18: Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
ESV.19: Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. And there was one governor who was over the land.
ESV.20: Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea. They ate and drank and were happy.
ESV.21: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates  to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
ESV.22: Solomon's provision for one day was thirty cors  of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,
ESV.23: ten fat oxen, and twenty pasture-fed cattle, a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.
ESV.24: For he had dominion over all the region west of the Euphrates  from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the Euphrates. And he had peace on all sides around him.
ESV.25: And Judah and Israel lived in safety, from Dan even to Beersheba, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, all the days of Solomon.
ESV.26: Solomon also had 40,000  stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.
ESV.27: And those officers supplied provisions for King Solomon, and for all who came to King Solomon's table, each one in his month. They let nothing be lacking.
ESV.28: Barley also and straw for the horses and swift steeds they brought to the place where it was required, each according to his duty.
ESV.29: And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding beyond measure, and breadth of mind like the sand on the seashore,
ESV.30: so that Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
ESV.31: For he was wiser than all other men, wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol, and his fame was in all the surrounding nations.
ESV.32: He also spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs were 1,005.
ESV.33: He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also of beasts, and of birds, and of reptiles, and of fish.
ESV.34: And people of all nations came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and from all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

NASB.1: Now King Solomon was king over all Israel.
NASB.2: These were his officials: Azariah the son of Zadok [was] the priest;
NASB.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha [were] secretaries; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud [was] the recorder;
NASB.4: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada [was] over the army; and Zadok and Abiathar [were] priests;
NASB.5: and Azariah the son of Nathan [was] over the deputies; and Zabud the son of Nathan, a priest, [was] the king's friend;
NASB.6: and Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram the son of Abda [was] over the men subject to forced labor.
NASB.7: Solomon had twelve deputies over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household; each man had to provide for a month in the year.
NASB.8: These are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
NASB.9: Ben-deker in Makaz and Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elonbeth-hanan;
NASB.10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth (Socoh [was] his and all the land of Hepher);
NASB.11: Ben-abinadab, [in] all the height of Dor (Taphath the daughter of Solomon was his wife);
NASB.12: Baana the son of Ahilud, [in] Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah as far as the other side of Jokmeam;
NASB.13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead (the towns of Jair, the son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead were his: the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars [were] his);
NASB.14: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, [in] Mahanaim;
NASB.15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he also married Basemath the daughter of Solomon);
NASB.16: Baana the son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
NASB.17: Jehoshaphat the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
NASB.18: Shimei the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
NASB.19: Geber the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and [he was] the only deputy who [was] in the land.
NASB.20: Judah and Israel [were] as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore in abundance; [they] were eating and drinking and rejoicing.
NASB.21: Now Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River [to] the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt; [they] brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
NASB.22: Solomon's provision for one day was thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,
NASB.23: ten fat oxen, twenty pasture-fed oxen, a hundred sheep besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.
NASB.24: For he had dominion over everything west of the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings west of the River; and he had peace on all sides around about him.
NASB.25: So Judah and Israel lived in safety, every man under his vine and his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
NASB.26: Solomon had 40,000 stalls of horses for his chariots, and 12,000 horsemen.
NASB.27: Those deputies provided for King Solomon and all who came to King Solomon's table, each in his month; they left nothing lacking.
NASB.28: They also brought barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the place where it should be, each according to his charge.
NASB.29: Now God gave Solomon wisdom and very great discernment and breadth of mind, like the sand that is on the seashore.
NASB.30: Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the sons of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
NASB.31: For he was wiser than all men, than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and his fame was [known] in all the surrounding nations.
NASB.32: He also spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs were 1,005.
NASB.33: He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows on the wall; he spoke also of animals and birds and creeping things and fish.
NASB.34: Men came from all peoples to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

NKJV.1: So King Solomon was king over all Israel.

NKJV.13: Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead; to him belonged the towns of Jair the son of Manasseh, in Gilead; to him also belonged the region of Argob in Bashan—sixty large cities with walls and bronze gate-bars;
NKJV.14: Ahinadab the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

WEB.22: Solomon’s provision for one day was thirty cors  of fine flour, sixty measures of meal,
WEB.23: ten head of fat cattle, twenty head of cattle out of the pastures, and one hundred sheep, besides deer, and gazelles, and roebucks, and fattened fowl.
WEB.24: For he had dominion over all on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza, over all the kings on this side the River: and he had peace on all sides around him.
WEB.25: Judah and Israel lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
WEB.26: Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
WEB.27: Those officers provided food for king Solomon, and for all who came to king Solomon’s table, every man in his month. They let nothing be lacking.
WEB.28: They also brought Barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds to the place where the officers were, each man according to his duty.
WEB.29: God gave Solomon abundant wisdom and understanding, and very great understanding, even as the sand that is on the seashore.
WEB.30: Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.
WEB.31: For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all the nations all around.
WEB.32: He spoke three thousand proverbs; and his songs numbered one thousand five.
WEB.33: He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he also spoke of animals, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish.
WEB.34: People of all nations came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, sent by all kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.

CSB17.1: King Solomon reigned over all Israel, <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.2: and these were his officials: ⓛ Azariah son of Zadok, priest;
CSB17.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah the sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, court historian;
CSB17.4: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, in charge of the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
CSB17.5: Azariah son of Nathan, in charge of the deputies; Zabud son of Nathan, a priest and adviser to the king;
CSB17.6: Ahishar, in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda, in charge of forced labor.
CSB17.7: Solomon had twelve deputies for all Israel. They provided food for the king and his household; each one made provision for one month out of the year. <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.8: These were their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
CSB17.9: Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
CSB17.10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth (he had Socoh and the whole land of Hepher);
CSB17.11: Ben-abinadab, in all Naphath-dor (Taphath daughter of Solomon was his wife);
CSB17.12: Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shean which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as the other side of Jokmeam;
CSB17.13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead (he had the villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, and he had the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars);
CSB17.14: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
CSB17.15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he also had married a daughter of Solomon — Basemath);
CSB17.16: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
CSB17.17: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
CSB17.18: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
CSB17.19:
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of King Sihon of the Amorites and of King Og of Bashan.
There was one deputy in the land of Judah. [1]
CSB17.20: Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand by the sea; <sup>ⓝ</sup> they were eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
CSB17.21: Solomon ruled all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt. <sup>ⓐ</sup> They offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.22: Solomon’s provisions for one day were 150 bushels <sup>[2]</sup> of fine flour and 300 bushels <sup>[3]</sup> of meal,
CSB17.23: ten fattened cattle, twenty range cattle, and a hundred sheep and goats, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and pen-fed poultry, <sup>[4]</sup> <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.24: for he had dominion over everything west of the Euphrates from Tiphsah to Gaza and over all the kings west of the Euphrates. He had peace on all his surrounding borders.
CSB17.25: Throughout Solomon’s reign, Judah and Israel lived in safety from Dan to Beer-sheba, <sup>ⓓ</sup> each person under his own vine and his own fig tree. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.26: Solomon had forty thousand <sup>[5]</sup> stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.27: Each of those deputies for a month in turn provided food for King Solomon and for everyone who came to King Solomon’s table. They neglected nothing.
CSB17.28: Each man brought the barley and the straw for the chariot teams and the other horses <sup>ⓖ</sup> to the required place according to his assignment. <sup>[6]</sup>
CSB17.29: God gave Solomon wisdom, very great insight, and understanding <sup>ⓗ</sup> as vast as the sand on the seashore.
CSB17.30: Solomon’s wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the people of the East, <sup>ⓘ</sup> greater than all the wisdom of Egypt. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.31: He was wiser than anyone <sup>ⓚ</sup>  — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, sons of Mahol. <sup>ⓜ</sup> His reputation extended to all the surrounding nations. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.32: Solomon spoke 3,000 proverbs, <sup>ⓐ</sup> and his songs numbered 1,005. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.33: He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing out of the wall. He also spoke about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.
CSB17.34: Emissaries of all peoples, sent by every king on earth who had heard of his wisdom, came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom. <sup>ⓒ</sup>

NLT.1: King Solomon now ruled over all Israel,
NLT.2: and these were his high officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest.
NLT.3:
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were court secretaries.
Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian.
NLT.4:
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was commander of the army.
Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
NLT.5:
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the district governors.
Zabud son of Nathan, a priest, was a trusted adviser to the king.
NLT.6:
Ahishar was manager of the palace property.
Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of forced labor.
NLT.7: Solomon also had twelve district governors who were over all Israel. They were responsible for providing food for the king’s household. Each of them arranged provisions for one month of the year.
NLT.8: These are the names of the twelve governors: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim.
NLT.9: Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-bethhanan.
NLT.10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth, including Socoh and all the land of Hepher.
NLT.11: Ben-abinadab, in all of Naphoth-dor. (He was married to Taphath, one of Solomon’s daughters.)
NLT.12: Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, all of Beth-shan near Zarethan below Jezreel, and all the territory from Beth-shan to Abel-meholah and over to Jokmeam.
NLT.13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead, including the Towns of Jair (named for Jair of the tribe of Manasseh ) in Gilead, and in the Argob region of Bashan, including sixty large fortified towns with bronze bars on their gates.
NLT.14: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim.
NLT.15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali. (He was married to Basemath, another of Solomon’s daughters.)
NLT.16: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and in Aloth.
NLT.17: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar.
NLT.18: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin.
NLT.19:
Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, including the territories of King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan.
There was also one governor over the land of Judah.
NLT.20: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They were very contented, with plenty to eat and drink.
NLT.21: Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of the Philistines and the border of Egypt in the south. The conquered peoples of those lands sent tribute money to Solomon and continued to serve him throughout his lifetime.
NLT.22: The daily food requirements for Solomon’s palace were 150 bushels of choice flour and 300 bushels of meal ;
NLT.23: also 10 oxen from the fattening pens, 20 pasture-fed cattle, 100 sheep or goats, as well as deer, gazelles, roe deer, and choice poultry.
NLT.24: Solomon’s dominion extended over all the kingdoms west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza. And there was peace on all his borders.
NLT.25: During the lifetime of Solomon, all of Judah and Israel lived in peace and safety. And from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, each family had its own home and garden.
NLT.26: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses, and he had 12,000 horses.
NLT.27: The district governors faithfully provided food for King Solomon and his court; each made sure nothing was lacking during the month assigned to him.
NLT.28: They also brought the necessary barley and straw for the royal horses in the stables.
NLT.29: God gave Solomon very great wisdom and understanding, and knowledge as vast as the sands of the seashore.
NLT.30: In fact, his wisdom exceeded that of all the wise men of the East and the wise men of Egypt.
NLT.31: He was wiser than anyone else, including Ethan the Ezrahite and the sons of Mahol — Heman, Calcol, and Darda. His fame spread throughout all the surrounding nations.
NLT.32: He composed some 3,000 proverbs and wrote 1,005 songs.
NLT.33: He could speak with authority about all kinds of plants, from the great cedar of Lebanon to the tiny hyssop that grows from cracks in a wall. He could also speak about animals, birds, small creatures, and fish.
NLT.34: And kings from every nation sent their ambassadors to listen to the wisdom of Solomon.

NET.2: These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest.
NET.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, wrote down what happened. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was in charge of the records.
NET.4: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was commander of the army. Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
NET.5: Azariah son of Nathan was supervisor of the district governors. Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and adviser to the king.
NET.6: Ahishar was supervisor of the palace. Adoniram son of Abda was supervisor of the work crews.
NET.7: Solomon had twelve district governors appointed throughout Israel who acquired supplies for the king and his palace. Each was responsible for one month in the year.
NET.8: These were their names: Ben-Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
NET.9: Ben-Deker was in charge of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan.
NET.10: Ben-Hesed was in charge of Arubboth; he controlled Socoh and all the territory of Hepher.
NET.11: Ben-Abinadab was in charge of Naphath Dor. (He was married to Solomon’s daughter Taphath.)
NET.12: Baana son of Ahilud was in charge of Taanach and Megiddo, as well as all of Beth Shan next to Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shan to Abel Meholah and on past Jokmeam.
NET.13: Ben-Geber was in charge of Ramoth Gilead; he controlled the tent villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan, including sixty large walled cities with bronze bars locking their gates.
NET.14: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of Mahanaim.
NET.15: Ahimaaz was in charge of Naphtali. (He married Solomon’s daughter Basemath.)
NET.16: Baana son of Hushai was in charge of Asher and Aloth.
NET.17: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of Issachar.
NET.18: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of Benjamin.
NET.19: Geber son of Uri was in charge of the land of Gilead (the territory which had once belonged to King Sihon of the Amorites and to King Og of Bashan). He was sole governor of the area.
NET.20: The people of Judah and Israel were as innumerable as the sand on the seashore; they had plenty to eat and drink and were happy.
NET.21: (5:1) Solomon ruled all the kingdoms from the Euphrates River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms paid tribute as Solomon’s subjects throughout his lifetime.
NET.22: Each day Solomon’s royal court consumed thirty cors of finely milled flour, sixty cors of cereal,
NET.23: ten calves fattened in the stall, twenty calves from the pasture, and a hundred sheep, not to mention rams, gazelles, deer, and well-fed birds.
NET.24: His royal court was so large because he ruled over all the kingdoms west of the Euphrates River from Tiphsah to Gaza; he was at peace with all his neighbors.
NET.25: All the people of Judah and Israel had security; everyone from Dan to Beer Sheba enjoyed the produce of their vines and fig trees throughout Solomon’s lifetime.
NET.26: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.
NET.27: The district governors acquired supplies for King Solomon and all who ate in his royal palace. Each was responsible for one month in the year; they made sure nothing was lacking.
NET.28: Each one also brought to the assigned location his quota of barley and straw for the various horses.
NET.29: God gave Solomon wisdom and very great discernment; the breadth of his understanding was as infinite as the sand on the seashore.
NET.30: Solomon was wiser than all the men of the east and all the sages of Egypt.
NET.31: He was wiser than any man, including Ethan the Ezrahite or Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. He was famous in all the neighboring nations.
NET.33: He produced manuals on botany, describing every kind of plant, from the cedars of Lebanon to the hyssop that grows on walls. He also produced manuals on biology, describing animals, birds, insects, and fish.
NET.34: People from all nations came to hear Solomon’s display of wisdom; they came from all the kings of the earth who heard about his wisdom.
